title: Ackermann Function
domain: Nonnegative integer pairs in the tested table range; deep inputs may exhaust the interpreter's activation resources.
description: Compute the two-argument Ackermann function with the unoptimized recursive definition. No memoisation, closed-form shortcuts, MASM acceleration or language changes are used.
attribution: Problem and REBOL reference: Rosetta Code, 'Ackermann function' (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Ackermann_function). The REBOL listing is the unoptimized case-based solution shown on that page; the Glon implementation is original for this challenge.
reference: Expected values are the mathematical Ackermann table for m=0..3 and n=0..4, supplied as expected results rather than inferred from previous Glon runs. Each case runs in its own bounded process.
family_note: Rosetta Code challenge; separate from the REBOL Cookbook file-replacement challenge.

resource_probes.observed: exit 1; machine halt before producing the expected 125; no SIN!
resource_probes.note: Resource-limit probe, not a correctness case. The unoptimized recursion exhausts interpreter activation/return-stack resources on the pinned 64K interpreter.

known_limitations: The tested correctness range is m=0..3 with n=0..4 except (3,4): 19/20 expected values pass.
A(3,4)=125 is mathematically expected but fail-stops with a machine-level halt (not a SIN!) on the pinned 64K interpreter; it is recorded as a resource probe, not a passing correctness test.
The unoptimized definition has no memoisation or closed-form shortcuts as required; larger inputs were not pursued to find the maximum recursion depth.
Fail-stops are machine-level and cannot be caught with judge.

reference_implementation.title: Ackermann function — REBOL solution shown on Rosetta Code
reference_implementation.attribution: Rosetta Code, Ackermann function, REBOL solution (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Ackermann_function).
reference_implementation.notes: Unoptimized case-based recursive definition; the page also shows a separate optimized small-m variant, which is not used here.

rebol.observable_behaviour: Returns the Ackermann value for nonnegative m,n, subject to the REBOL runtime's recursion limits.
rebol.facilities: func, case, arithmetic, comparison and recursion from REBOL 2.
rebol.test_status: The original listing is preserved verbatim as reference source. It was not executed here; there is no REBOL 2 runtime in this repository.

glon.observable_behaviour: Returns the same values for the 19 tested pairs; (3,4) is a documented resource fail-stop.
glon.facilities: Ordinary Glon func/either, arithmetic/comparison and recursion; no memoisation, shortcut, MASM or new vocabulary.
glon.test_status: 19/20 mathematically expected table values passed in separate bounded processes; (3,4) is recorded as a resource probe.

implementation_comparison.notice: Both listings are application-level recursive definitions. Source sizes are descriptive, not a concision claim. The Glon resource limit is documented rather than hidden by an optimization.
